key_insight: Under identical conditions, the continuous-variable (CV) quantum head outperforms the discrete-variable (DV) head for wafer-map defect classification, indicating CV is the stronger paradigm for this structured vision task.
engineering_relevance: For semiconductor yield screening, the result suggests quantum models may be most useful when the quantum layer preserves spatial structure and phase-space continuity, especially for localized defect patterns.
method: Shared ~4.3M-parameter convolutional backbone used for all models
Interchangeable heads: classical dense, CV-QNN, or DV-QNN
Quantum head size scaled across 3, 4, and 8 qumodes/qubits
evidence_signal: On WM-811K (8 classes), the 4-unit CV model reached 79.7% ± 1.8% accuracy versus 61.6% ± 1.4% for DV, with the strongest class-level gain on Edge-Loc recall (0.66 ± 0.06 vs. ≤0.05).
watch_item: The comparison is still limited by hardware noise and a shallow DV setup, and both quantum heads remain below the 85.0% classical baseline.
paper_title: Bridging Quantum Computing Paradigms toward Semiconductor Yield: A Controlled CV-versus-DV Comparison on Wafer-Map Defect Classification
